headline: Easy-run HR improvement has held for a second block while volume stayed sharply elevated.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The aerobic efficiency gain flagged yesterday isn't a one-day artefact — it's holding across a run of comparable easy efforts even as your 4-week volume sits well above the prior block. That combination is the meaningful signal today: normally a large volume jump pushes easy HR up, and instead it's settled lower. This is consistent with a genuine aerobic adaptation rather than a favourable sampling of easy days.

Worth noticing that recent easy paces have drifted a touch slower even as HR dropped, which is a reasonable trade-off while you're absorbing a big load — you're banking durability and time on feet rather than chasing pace right now. Your fast end is still demonstrated (the late-June threshold-type effort), so this isn't a loss of speed, just a deliberate skew toward the endurance side ahead of a long self-supported stretch in August.

Strength frequency has stabilised at the same level as the prior block rather than drifting further, which resolves part of what was flagged last week — the running load hasn't crowded it out. Zone 2 has also climbed back to the bottom of the target band, so the earlier gap looks more like distribution than a structural hole.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR stays low if easy paces start creeping back toward previous levels — that's the cleaner confirmation of the adaptation.
Note whether the pace-for-HR trade-off shifts as this volume block matures or you back off slightly.
Keep an eye on strength frequency holding steady rather than slipping now that running load is high.
As sleep tracking accumulates, watch for any link between low-score nights and next-day aerobic HR.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 164 km vs 92 km prior block (+79%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 143 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 6 runs)
▲ Zone 2: 189 min vs 180-240 min/week target (105% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 0.3%
